study type: Double-blind randomized controlled study with a reference group
outcome: Expression of microbial genes related to reactive oxygen species metabolism
Expression of microbial genes related to lipopolysaccharide biosynthesis
Expression of microbial genes related to milk carbohydrate metabolism
cohort: The study included 153 infants born by elective C-section, randomized to receive different infant formulas, and a reference group of vaginally born infants.
finding: The synbiotic formula modulated the expression of microbial genes involved in (oligo)saccharide metabolism, creating a hypoxic and acidic gut environment that prevented the establishment of a compromised microbiome, thus emulating the eco-physiological gut environment observed in vaginally born infants.
mod_finding: As early as day 3, vaginally born infants presented a hypoxic and acidic gut environment with enriched strict anaerobes, while C-section born infants exhibited a compromised microbiome with Enterobacteriaceae and signatures of an oxygen-rich gut, enriched with genes for reactive oxygen species metabolism and lipopolysaccharide biosynthesis.
followup_time: 22 weeks (from birth until 4 months old for intervention, stool samples collected till week 22)
